about: The phone's history (docs/plan.md slice 15; the charts brief, decided 2026-09-30): QuestPumpCore's HistoryPump.group, HistorySeries.build, HistorySync and GameCalendar, and the Android core's, implement every section; the correction case is the addon's fold (DB.lua) too. Rows are history rows (GET /v1/history's, the fields the phone keeps), sheets are {char, sheet} with the addon's sheet summary (Stats.lua ns.SheetSummary). Times are unix seconds. A game day is the date, in the zone, of the time minus dayOffsetH hours. A performed move is a row of kind 1-4 with outcome 1-6 or 11; an offered pump a row of kind 5 or 6 with outcome 7, a device pump one with flag bit 4 (watch), 7 (phone) or 12 (computer, the desktop app's catch-up, slice 35) without bit 11 (the app's own row). Rows are read sorted by row_ts (stable). A correction (kind 7) names its row by row_ts, quest_id, slot and move; of the corrections naming one row, in rows and app_rows alike (one map since slice 44, as every fold reads them: DB.lua ns.CorrectionBeats), the one of the highest round (its outcome) wins, of two of one round the smaller reps, then the smaller seconds, and of rows of round 0 (written before the rounds) the last in the given order, rows first, then app_rows; it sets a performed move row's count (a hold's seconds, a pose's answer and any other kind's reps, the other field kept), never a timed cardio row's (a cardio row without flag bit 10) nor a stopped row's (outcome 6), which no correction changes, and the row then counts as typed, but for a count of 0 (a hold's 0 s), which reads as typing 0 does, done without a count: no typed attempt and no count (slice 44's review, 2026-10-18; DB.lua correct). A censored row (outcome 4) whose stored count (a hold's seconds, any other kind's reps) equals its window's top (contract/library.json: the hi of its ladder's rung, the rung-th of that ladder's rungs, or of the move's own window in that rung's alt where it has one) is a capped max set, which keeps that count for a correction at or over it and takes one under it; any other censored row, a long set, takes its correction whatever it is (slice 44's review; DB.lua ns.CappedSet, whose fold also asks that the move held no record before the set or its ladder was being placed again, which only a fold of the whole save can tell: a long set that stopped exactly at its top is the one censored row a reader without that fold reads otherwise). A typed attempt is a rep or hold row with outcome 1-4 or 11, or a corrected one (but one corrected to 0, which reads done without a count). An hr_verdict other than proven, unproven or no_hr reads as no verdict. pumps (newest first): count is the pump row's reps, a level-up's (ding) the moves grouped under it; reps on a typed rep move and on a counted set (a cardio row with flag bit 10), whose reps are its count (as corrected) above 0 whatever its outcome (2026-10-19, the program's double-check: one saved Form slipped is done with its count, outcome 5), null with none (counted and slipped tell such a move apart: the Saga words it as the game's Log does, its count or Not counted, and "form slipped" after either where slipped); counted true on a counted set and slipped true on one whose answer in flag bits 14-15 is 1, Form slipped (a steady cardio row's answer there is its pace, never slipped), each false where an expected move leaves it out (since 2026-10-19; until then such a set's reps were null unless its count was a typed attempt, so the Saga read a slipped 12 as a clock and an uncounted window as its seconds); record on a move stored with outcome 1 that no correction names (the Log's "a new record"); banked on a pump that a banked pump row (kind 5 or 6, outcome 9, its reason in flag bits 0-2 other than 4, felt unwell) follows before the next offered pump row (the Log's banked game pump); unwell on a pump that a felt-unwell row (UnwellLock.locks: a move row other than a paid one, or a kind 5 or 6 row banked, whose reason in flag bits 0-2 is 4) follows before the next offered pump row; source the pump row's PumpSource by its device bits (with the app bit 11: watch with bit 4, computer with bit 12, else phone; without it: catchUp with bit 4, 7 or 12, else game), watch its bit 4 and computer its bit 12 (slice 35); each its default (false, source game) where an expected pump leaves it out. desktop (where a case gives it; slice 35, HistoryPump.desktop, the one owner of the desktop app's pumps): the groups (HistoryPump.group) of the app_rows with bit 12 that hold a performed move or are unwell, newest first, each by its id, moves and unwell (false where left out); one left with neither (a pump opened in the desktop app and left before its first move) is none and counts nowhere. catch_ups (the catch-ups the phone keeps, [] when it is absent: start, moves, watch; slice 34, LogPumps.held): a catch-up and a device pump row whose watch bit (4) is its watch and whose row_ts lies within 120 s of its start pair up nearest first (of two as near, the earlier row, then the earlier catch-up), each once, and the row holds it; one that no row holds counts as a free pump does in days (a pump and its moves) and its moves as catchUp in its week, and its start is an input time. days: the game days with a performed move, an offered pump, a free pump, a catch-up no row holds or an app row's record; records: rows stored with outcome 1 that no correction names, and the input's app_rows (the app's own rows, [] when it is absent) of a performed move stored with outcome 1 that no correction names (a correction in rows or app_rows), which add no pump and no move (those are the free pumps'), but for a desktop app pump's (slice 35: an offered pump row with flag bit 12, which no phone keeps as a free pump): it and the performed moves grouped under it (HistoryPump.desktop) count as a free pump does, in days (a pump and its moves) and its moves as free in its week, its row_ts an input time; step 0 without moves, 1 below mapSteps[0], 2 below mapSteps[1], else 3. A game week holds seven game days from the one the weekly reset falls in, from the ws of the newest readable sheet (by at) that has one: week k (floor(d / 7), d the dates from ws's game day to t's) starts at the dayOffsetH:00 wall clock of the date 7k days after ws's game day, so the reset's own game day belongs to the week it starts from its 04:00 on and a week across a clock change still holds seven dates (slice 34); the gains and muscleWeeks bin at the reset itself, floor((t - ws) / 604800), each at the start of the game week of that number; without one, the game weeks outside WoW (slice 27): Monday to Sunday by game days, each from dayOffsetH:00 on its Monday's wall clock in the zone (a week across a clock change runs 167 or 169 hours), from the week of the game day holding the first time among the rows, free pumps, catch-ups no row holds and health spans (or now, with none of them). weeks: every week from the first input's to the later of now's and the last input's, [] without an input; game, catchUp and free count moves done, never pumps (David, 2026-10-27: "Instead of pumps count moves please"; each pump until then): every performed move row counts 1 in the week of its own row_ts, as catchUp when its pump, the offered pump row latest before it in the sorted rows, is a device pump, else as game (as well with no offered pump before it); an offered pump row adds nothing; a free pump adds its moves to free in the week of its start, a catch-up no row holds its moves to catchUp and a desktop app pump its moves to free (as above), so a week's game, catchUp and free sum to its days' moves; minutes take the union of the health spans (time two spans share counts once), each merged span's seconds in the week it starts, the week's sum / 60, rounded down. A sheet this build cannot read (no at, a list where a number belongs) stays kept but no series reads it. The sheet series take each game day's last readable sheet of all characters merged and keep a point only when its value changes (the first always; a ladder's value is its rung, move, record and stars); gains and muscleWeeks take each week's last readable sheet (at = the week's start, every week's point kept). stats, gains, ladders, quality and muscleWeeks have as many series as the widest such list among the readable sheets, and a sheet whose list is shorter gives no point for the index it lacks; without a readable sheet they are [] or {}. level is lvl + into / need in doubles (lvl when need is 0); ladders, quality and muscleWeeks are keyed by id as a string; a muscle's quality is its mq on a v 3 sheet (0 none, 1 Starter ... 6 Legendary) and, for a trained muscle, one more than a v 1 or v 2 sheet's, which had no Starter (0 stays none). sync: HistorySync.step, kept being the store and the item count the phone keeps for that log: append when it keeps no store and no items and asked from 0, or when the page's store is the kept one and its next is at least the asked after; anything else is restart, rows kept under no store (items above 0) too, so they merge through restart. restart: HistorySync.restart(old:fresh:), the kept rows dated before the new store's oldest row that carries its own time (a paid row, outcome 10, and a correction, kind 7, carry the time of the row they name; with no such row, no bound) and at or after its latest reset row, less one kept row for each equal new row (one for one), then the new store's rows; latest_reset: HistorySync.latestReset of the rows kept after it, the newest reset row's time, or null. sheet_restart: HistorySync.restart(old:fresh:reset:), the readable kept sheets before the new log's oldest (all of them when it is empty) and at or after reset, then the new log's; prune: HistorySync.dropBefore(reset:sheets:), the kept sheets at or after reset, the unreadable ones dropped, all kept when reset is null; proofs: HistorySync.apply(proofs:to:), the last proof of a row_ts replacing all three hr fields; proofs_since: HistorySync.proofsSince(rows:now:), the row_ts of the oldest offered pump row without a verdict (an unknown verdict is none), never earlier than now - 1,209,600 s (14 days) nor later than now - 86,400 s (1 day), which it is when every offered pump has a verdict; recover: HistorySync.recover(fileLines:cursorLines:), cursor_lines when the kept file holds at least that many good lines, else null (start over from after=0); calendar: GameCalendar.build(days:weeks:ws:zone:dayOffsetH:now:) from a series' days and weeks (ascending): current is now's week, from HistorySeries.weekStart(now, ws) (with a ws the start of the game week holding now, as above; without one dayOffsetH:00 on the wall clock of the Monday of the week of now's game day), there without days too, and weeks the weeks newest first from it back (weekStart of the week back weeks before) up to and including the first that holds a day at or before the first of days, at most 13, [] without days. A week is {start, days: the seven dates from the date of start - dayOffsetH hours in the zone, each {day (the date, never the game day of its 04:00), step and record (its entry of days: step, records > 0; 0 and false without one), today (now's game day), future (a later date)}, game, catchUp and app (the game, catchUp and free of the series week with that start, its moves by where they were done; 0 without one), minutes (its minutes), moves and records (the sums of its seven days' entries)}. saga (the Saga's day, 2026-10-15): its own about states the rules of a day's chapter, best day and quality, its strip, records, unlocks, hero move and week. log (slice 44, LogPumps.build): its own about states how the Log and the Saga list a game pump from what the phone and the wrist kept of it, before and after its rows come.

cases.about: Zurich over the October change, no sheet with ws. Corrections: the push-ups typed 14 (a beat) are corrected to 12 and then 13 (the last wins), the plank's 40 s to 35 s, an untyped chair squat (Done with an empty box) to 9, which then counts as typed; the chair stand stays untyped. A corrected beat is no record (20 October shows 0 records: the phone cannot classify the corrected count). Read last: a correction naming the march in place, a timed cardio row, which changes nothing (no correction changes one, since slice 44; the Log shows no count for a move done by its seconds either), and the glute bridges' typed 8 corrected to 0, which reads as typing 0 does, done without a count: no attempt and no count in the Log (slice 44's review). All of them arrive after later pumps' rows. The pump at 03:30 CET on Sunday 25 October, after the clocks went back at 03:00 CEST, is already that game day (4 h earlier is 00:30 CEST), the one at 03:30 on Monday 26 October is still Sunday's game day and so in the first week, as is the sheet folded two minutes later (each week starts at 04:00 on its Monday in the zone: 19 October 04:00 CEST, then 26 October 04:00 CET, 169 hours on), so gains and muscleWeeks hold the first week's point alone, from that later sheet; the week of 2 November is empty. The addon's fold of these rows gives the same records as the attempts. Its sheets are v 1 (folded before 2026-10-01): each reads with its third and fourth stats swapped and no crit.

Los Angeles: a pump at 02:30 on Tuesday belongs to Monday's game day, as does a move row whose pump row fell out of the ring (it belongs to no pump, and its week counts it as game). An old save's level-up pump; an owed plank the watch's catch-up pays; a banked pump (an offered pump with no move done, step 0, banked: its banked pump row, with a reason from before 2026-10-04, follows it) whose squats the phone's catch-up pays, read after the evening's pump, and whose cardio move the computer's catch-up pays on 15 October (bit 12: a device pump, so its week counts the move as catchUp); a stretch row and a rung row, which are no moves. Two characters' sheets merged, the older without ws, two on Friday 2 October (the later one wins); the anchor is the newest sheet's ws (Tuesday 13 October 15:00 UTC), so earlier weeks have negative indices (floor, not truncation). The free pump at 07:59 PDT on Tuesday 29 September, a minute before that week's reset, is on the reset's game day and so in the week it starts (slice 34), as are the 3 minutes of its Health span; the minutes sum a week's seconds before dividing (90 + 90 + 75 s is 4 minutes); 14 October reaches step 3 at exactly 10 moves. The phone keeps five catch-ups: the watch's at 11:59:58 on Thursday 1 October, which the watch's catch-up rows two seconds later hold; another of the watch's a minute later, which that row cannot hold too (one to one); the phone's at 12:00:30 that day, near the watch's row but without its bit; the phone's at 12:02 on Friday 2 October, which the phone's catch-up rows hold at the window's edge, 120 s before it; and the phone's at 04:10 on Friday 9 October, which no row holds (the helper found nothing owed). The three no row holds count as catch-up pumps with their moves: 1 October's two make it 4 pumps and 5 moves, step 2, and 9 October's two moves are the only ones in the week of 6 October. The gains and the muscle weeks bin at the reset itself and each stands at the start of the game week of the same number (04:00 PDT on its Tuesday, 4 hours before the reset), where the series' weeks start. Its sheets are v 1 (folded before 2026-10-01): each reads with its third and fourth stats swapped and no crit.

Kolkata (UTC+05:30), rows only, no sheets: every sheet series is empty ([] and {}). An old save's level-up pump whose ding row carries the level (7) in reps counts the 2 moves grouped under it. A pump row whose hr_verdict is one this build does not know ("future") reads as no verdict: not proven. A pump dated two weeks after now (the phone's clock behind the game's) keeps its game day and its week: the weeks run from the first input's to the later of now's and the last input's, the week between them empty. The fallback anchor is Monday 5 October 04:00 IST (22:30 UTC on Sunday).

New York, sheets only: no row, free pump or health span, so days and weeks are [] and the fallback anchor is the Monday of now's week (23 November 04:00 EST); no sheet sets it. Of the five sheets two do not read and are skipped by every series: one without at, and the newest, whose lvl is a list where a number belongs (its ws, Tuesday 24 November 15:00 UTC, would move the anchor if it were read). A second character's sheet from an older addon has four stats, six ladders and eighteen muscles: the series count follows the widest readable list (5, 7, 19), and the shorter sheet adds no point for an index it lacks (stat 5's gains and muscle 19's weeks skip its week; ladder 7 and muscle 19's quality keep their value across it, so the next sheet adds no point there either). Its sheets are v 1 (folded before 2026-10-01): each reads with its third and fourth stats swapped and no crit.

Tokyo, rows, free pumps and health spans that overlap, no sheets: the minutes count the union of the spans, never time two spans share twice. The watch's play session from 19:00 to 20:00 on Tuesday 3 November holds the phone's free pump at 19:20 (4 minutes) and overlaps the next one, 19:50 to 20:05: 65 minutes, not 79. Thursday's 125 s free pump adds to them before the week's seconds are divided (127 minutes in the first week). The session from 03:30 to 04:30 on Monday 9 November starts in the first week, so the free pump at 04:10 inside it adds no minute anywhere: merged into the session, it counts in the week the merged span starts, while the pump itself counts in the second week (its game day, Monday, and its moves as free). The spans arrive in no order. Weeks run from Monday 2 November 04:00 JST to now's week, 16 November. The app's own rows add no record (records, never a pump or a move, which the free pumps count): on Monday a correction names the beat (15 corrected to 12), and on Thursday the game names the app pump's push-ups typed 13 (a beat), corrected to 14 (round 1): one map over both stores (slice 44). The game's push-ups typed 11 on Tuesday (a beat) were corrected in the game to 10 (round 1) and, before the two heard of each other, on the phone to 9 (round 1, in app_rows): of one round the smaller count wins, 9, everywhere, and the game's /qp undo to 8 (round 0, written before the rounds and last in rows) loses to round 1; so no day holds a record.

UTC, the desktop app's pumps alone (slice 35): its rows as a phone keeps the helper's copy of them (bit 12, the app bit cleared), no game row, free pump, sheet or health span. A pump opened at 10:00 on Tuesday 27 October and left on Ready (its offered row alone) is none: no day, no week and no input time, so the weeks start on Monday 2 November. The pump at 18:00 on Tuesday 3 November with the push-ups typed 14 (a beat, a record) and a timed cardio move counts as a free pump with its 2 moves, and the one at 09:00 on Thursday 5 November that its felt-unwell stop ends before its first move (a pump row banked for feeling unwell) as a free pump with none, unwell, as the phone keeps its own stopped pump. Now is Saturday 7 November 12:00.

UTC, rows only, censored sets corrected (slice 44's review, 2026-10-18). The push-ups' first max set, stored censored at its window's top (40: the push ladder's first rung, contract/library.json) and corrected to 46, keeps 40: a capped max set keeps its top for a correction at or over it. The next day's 50 is a record. The third day's long set, stored censored at 45 (past censor_s under the record before it) and corrected to 52, takes 52: its stored count is not its window's top, so it takes its correction (the rule before the review kept a censored set's stored count for any correction over it, 45). Both corrections arrive after the rows they name. The addon's fold of these rows gives the same counts and records (40, 50, 52).

sync.about: a phone that keeps nothing: any page appends and its store is kept
the next page of the same store
nothing new: an empty page of the same store
a reset compacted the store: a new name
the store shrank under the same name: an empty page whose next is below what was asked
the helper started an empty data folder
an empty helper and a phone that keeps nothing
rows kept under no store (the last read found the helper's store empty) and a store with rows: the store is read whole and merged through restart, never appended after the kept rows
rows kept under no store and the helper's store still empty: a restart too, which keeps every kept row
under a named store the kept items count for nothing (the phone keeps the history the helper lost beside the store's rows): the next page of the same store appends

restart.about: a new data folder: the kept rows dated before the new store's oldest row of its own time stay, in their order (a late paid row among them), then the new store's rows; the kept copy of a row the new store holds goes
a reset: the new store starts with its reset row, and every kept row before it goes
an empty new store keeps every kept row

a new data folder that took the phone's catch-up again (its confirmation was lost), then a correction: the new store's paid row (outcome 10) and correction (kind 7) carry the times of the rows they name, ten and five days back, and set no bound; its oldest row of its own time is the catch-up's pump, a day back. The kept rows before it stay, the owed plank at the paid row's time and the pump of five days back with its squats among them; the kept catch-up rows, dated at it, go; the kept paid row, equal to the new store's, goes once

a new store whose only row is a correction (the first thing typed under it repeats a count the kept log holds twice): no new row carries its own time, so no kept row is too new to stay, and one kept copy goes for the one equal new row, one for one, the other staying

two reset rows in the new store (a helper keeps only its latest, but the rule reads any rows): every kept row goes, the one dated between the resets and the one after the later too, since the earlier reset is the new store's oldest row of its own time and no kept row is both before it and at or after a reset; latest_reset is the later reset's time, not the first one listed

sheet_restart.about: a new data folder: the kept sheets folded before the new log's oldest sheet stay, then the new log's
a reset the rows hold (at T + 150): kept sheets older than it go, a kept sheet at or after it and older than the new log's oldest stays
a kept sheet this build cannot read has no readable at and goes, whether at is missing or a list stands where a number belongs (its raw at is never read)
an empty new sheet log keeps the kept sheets folded at or after the latest reset the rows hold (one folded at its very second stays), and none this build cannot read

prune.about: after the rows, a reset the kept rows hold (a save taken in whose sheet log did not start again): the kept sheets folded before it go, one folded at its very second stays, one this build cannot read goes
no reset among the kept rows: every kept sheet stays, one this build cannot read too

proofs.about: each proof reaches the pump row (kind 5 or 6, outcome offered) of its row_ts: a new verdict, a catch-up's (its move row of the same time is left alone), a newer verdict over an older one, a no_hr verdict without peak or delta; a proof naming no row changes nothing
the latest proof of a row_ts replaces all three fields: a no_hr proof clears the peak and the rise an older proof left on the kept row, and of two proofs for one row in a page the later wins

proofs_since.about: the oldest offered pump row without a verdict, inside the window: a level-up (ding) counts, the kept order is not the time order, and none of these counts: a pump with a verdict (proven, no_hr, or unproven, which is a verdict), a banked pump row (not offered), a move row
a pump without a verdict older than 14 days: never earlier than now - 14 days
every offered pump with a verdict: now - 1 day
the only pump without a verdict is two hours old: never later than now - 1 day
a verdict this build does not know reads as none: that pump is the oldest without a verdict

recover.about: the file holds what the cursor vouches for: the log goes on from the cursor
a page appended after the cursor was last written (the app ended between the file and the cursor): the lines past the cursor are dropped and fetched again, never kept twice
a file that lost a line, or holds one that does not read, holds fewer good lines than the cursor counts: that log starts over from after=0
the file is gone while its cursor stands: that log starts over from after=0
no cursor yet (or one that does not read, which counts as none): nothing in the file counts
a new phone: no file and no cursor

calendar.about: the Zurich case's days in Monday-first game weeks (no sheet names a reset), newest first: now's week (9 November, now on Wednesday 11 November: today the Wednesday, the days after it future) back to the week of the first day (19 October), four weeks; the week of the October clock change starts at 04:00 CET on Monday 26 October, 169 hours after the week before it; each week's game, catchUp and app (its moves by where they were done) and minutes are its HistorySeries week's, its moves and records its seven days'

at most 13 weeks: now is Monday 16 November 03:30 PST, still Sunday's game day, so now's week is 9 November (today its Sunday, nothing future) and the thirteenth is 17 August; the days on 30 June, 19 and 20 July fall before it and show nowhere; Sunday 1 November, the clock change, is the last day of the week of 26 October (which starts at 04:00 PDT); a day with a pump and no move (15 November) stays step 0 and adds nothing to its week's counts
a day after now's game day in now's week (a row dated after now) is future and keeps its step; now's week is the only one, so it is the current week too

the spring clock change (Zurich, Sunday 28 March 2027): the week holds seven dates, each cell named by its date (by the game day of its 04:00 start Sunday would read Saturday), so Sunday keeps its step and its record; now on Thursday 1 April, the days after it future; the week of 29 March starts 167 hours after the one before it

a paired player's weeks start on the game day the region's weekly reset the sheets name falls in (ws, Tuesday 3 November 15:00 UTC, 07:00 PST), at its 04:00, so each week's first day is a Tuesday and the series' weeks are kept under those starts; now on Wednesday 18 November 12:00 PST: now's week from Tuesday 17 November, today its Wednesday, back to the week of the first day (10 November)
no game day yet: no week of Pro's, and now's week for the week card, every day empty, today marked

saga.about: The Saga's day (2026-10-15; docs/plan.md's constants best_day_min_days, day_rank_days and day_rank_shares, exported in contract/library.json's constants, which `constants` repeats as these cases use them): one definition that four ports implement and are checked against once by a probe outside the repo: the game's fold (Stats.lua), the iPhone's QuestPumpCore beside HistorySeries, the Android core's, and the desktop app's desk/history.rs. Times are unix seconds; a game day is the date, in the zone, of the time less dayOffsetH hours (as everywhere); a day is written YYYY-MM-DD; times that tie keep the input's order (stable), and "later" means later in that order. A day's moves are the moves done from every source the surface holds (the game's rows, a catch-up's, the phone's and the watch's app pumps, the desktop app's), each counted once on the game day of its own time (a performed move row's row_ts, the fold's, the streak's and HistorySeries' rule, a level-up's moves too), so a pump across 04:00 gives each day its own moves; this is the one number Pump home's today and the game's Today tab show (the Saga's owner serves Pump home). A pump counts on a day once it has a move done that day. rank (rules 1-8; each case's days list every game day it knows with its moves, d the day ranked, possibly with days after it, which are never read): 1. an active day has moves >= 1; 2. chapter(d), only for an active d, is the number of active days dated at or before d (1 is the first; it never goes back), else null; 3. earlier(d) is the count of active days dated before d, of all the history the surface holds (the game's all-time sheet.activeDays counts today once today has a move: less one then); an app's rows may begin after the player's first days (the helper adopted a save whose ring had trimmed older rows), so an app adds to every chapter and earlier count the active days the game knows and its rows do not: the largest `ad` among its game sheets (a strip sheet's carries the save's baseline; the helper's own fold has none) less the active days the rows hold up to that sheet's game day, never below 0; 4. oldBest(d) is {moves, day}: the most moves on one active day before d, from every source, and the earliest day that reached it (a later equal day did not beat it), null when earlier(d) is 0 (the game's counts.maxMoves holds the game's rows alone and today too: never it); an app also weighs the `bd` of the game sheet that anchors it, the game's two best days of all time ([day, moves] each), those dated before d; 5. gate: earlier(d) >= best_day_min_days, without which d has no word and is no best day; 6. best (Best day ever): the gate, d active and moves(d) > oldBest(d).moves (a tie is no best day); 7. the window W is the active days e before d with 1 <= (d - e in calendar days) <= day_rank_days (the day day_rank_days before d is in it, the one before that is not), window its count, and above the days of W with more moves than d (an equal day is not above), both computed for every d; quality is null without the gate or for a d with no move; legendary for a best day (shown as Best day ever, never a word of its own); null when W is empty (a long break: the best day still reads all of history); else epic when above * 100 < day_rank_shares[0] * window, else rare when above * 100 < day_rank_shares[1] * window, else uncommon when above * 100 < day_rank_shares[2] * window, else common, compared in whole numbers (share = above / window as a real number: exactly 10 % is rare, 25 % uncommon, 50 % common); expected names moves(d), chapter, earlier, oldBest, gate, best, window, above and quality. 8. Today is live: today ranks as any day with its moves so far, so its word and its best day only rise as moves come; an earlier day's page ranks that day with its own moves against the days before it, as it stood at its end. strip (rules 9-11; zone, dayOffsetH, the game day `day`, and pumps, each {ts (its start), moves: [{move, ts (its own time), block, mp, ms}]} with the move's id and its block, mp and ms copied from contract/library.json): a pump with no move done on `day` draws nothing there; each other pump is one bar holding its moves of `day` alone, by block (strength, cardio, mobility, yoga, stacked in that order from the axis), in pump ts order; a bar stands at minute ((h - dayOffsetH) mod 24) * 60 + m of its pump's start's local wall clock (h, m; seconds dropped: 0 at 04:00, 1439 at 03:59) when the pump started on `day`, else (a pump begun the game day before) at minute 0; its bucket is by that same local hour h (minute 0: morning): morning 4 <= h < 12, afternoon 12 <= h < 17, evening 17 <= h < 22, night otherwise (22:00 to 03:59), and buckets sums each bucket's moves (a bucket with none shows no total); a platform draws the bars in minute order (then pump order) at one pitch for the day, the largest that keeps every bar at or right of its own start and inside the axis, the gap closing before the bars narrow (never under 1 px), each bar at its start or a pitch right of the one before, whichever is later, and shifts back left from the axis's end only what still passes it (tokens' DayStrip). On the night the clocks go back, the hour after 03:00 CET belongs to the new game day (its time less 4 h is past midnight) yet stands at the wall clock's 23:xx, night; on the night they go forward, the day before's game day runs to 05:00 local, so its 04:00-04:59 stands at minutes 0-59, morning. kinds counts the day's moves by block (the kinds bar, with the focus's ticks at contract/library.json constants.focus_share of the player's focus); muscles.most lists the body map's muscles (ids 1 to 16; 17 and up, the heart, the breath, balance, are none) that a move of the day names in mp, muscles.some those named only in ms (a muscle in both is most), ascending; moves and pumps count the day's moves and bars. highlights (rules 12-14; the day's performed move rows {ts, move, value (the typed count: a hold's seconds, a counted cardio set's count, else reps; null for a move done by its seconds alone), kg (a loaded set's weight in kg, from its load row; absent without one), record (stored as a record, outcome beat, which no correction names: the Log's a new record)}; before {move: its record as the fold held it at the day's start, since its latest clear or its ladder's start-over: a number, or {kg, reps} for a weighted record; absent without one}; the day's rung rows {ts, ladder, rung, cause (the row's reps, Progress.lua ns.RungCause: 1 up, 2 plateau, 3 down, 6 placementHigh and the rest), undone (a row /qp undo reversed)}; reached, the rungs ("ladder:rung") reached before the day from any source, a start-over included (it forgets none: Stats.lua markReached dates such a rung anew and calls the climb back Rekindled); start {ladder: the rung it started on}): 12. records, one row a move that has a record row that day, in the order of its first record row: best, its best set of the day (where the sets carry a weight, the one with the highest load score, kg x (load_epley + reps) as Progress.lua ns.LoadScore and ns.Classify compare them, given as {kg, reps}; else the most of its typed values), the earlier set keeping a tie, and was, before's value for it (null without one, then no was), each written as the Log writes it (a hold's m:ss, kg x reps); 13. unlocks, the steps the day reached for the first time, in ts order: a climb row (cause up 1, plateau 2, placementHigh 6 or check 9, a stretch check's lift, slice 42, which every port counts as the game's Stats.lua climbRow does since the program's double-check of 2026-10-19; not undone) that marks its rung reached as Stats.lua markReached does: a rung above the one its ladder started on and in neither reached nor an earlier unlock of the day (a climb back to a rung reached before, after a rung down or a start-over, is a Rekindled one, no unlock); each {ts, ladder, rung, move (the rung's anchor, the move contract/library.json marks anchor on that ladder and rung), quality (contract/library.json quality_by_step at the rung's step, plus 1: contract/sheet.json qualities' 1 Starter to 7 Artifact)}; an orange or gold rung a set earns later (its earns) is no unlock of its own; 14. the hero move (the knight on the page and the cards): the unlock of the highest quality, the later on a tie (heroFrom unlock); else the move of the day's last record row (record); else the move with the most rows that day, of two as many the one whose last row is later (most). 15. XP and level are a day's on the Saga's XP tile and the cards (the iPhone's LogList, Android's SagaBook, the desktop's desk/log.rs, the game's ns.DayTally): the XP the game's fold counted on that game day, by each gain's own row time, which a game sheet carries as `dx` ([day, XP] for each day with XP from `dxFrom`, the first game day it covers, the last dx_days game days at most, to its own day; a covered day absent from it gained none; the save is the account's, every character's, so never one character's sheets less another's), read from the surface's newest game sheet by its `at` (a strip sheet or the helper's own fold of the save that it serves, whichever is newer), a week's the sum of its days', and a day before `dxFrom` (or a week reaching before it) unknown: no XP and no level line; the level at the day's start from the sheet's lifetime XP less the XP of that day and every later day in `dx`, at its end less the later days' alone, through the level curve; `dxFrom` comes with or without `dx` (absent when no covered day gained XP); a sheet without `dxFrom` (an older addon) names no day's XP, and each day's level line is that day's newest sheet's level alone; with only the app's own sheet, where Hero shows it, today's XP alone, its start level from lifetime XP less today's through the level curve, and none on an earlier day or a week; the level at the day's start and end (Level 23 → 24, or Level 24 without a change), hidden when no sheet knows them, no case here; 16. the streak is the one the day ended with (the newest sheet of that day, any character's: the save is the account's), no case here. week (rule 17; zone, dayOffsetH, ws, the days and d): the game week holding d, its first day the Monday on or before d without a ws (ws null), else the game day of ws plus a whole number of weeks, the latest on or before d (floor((d - that day) / 7) weeks, back from a ws after d too), as the history's calendar weeks run (by dates, never the game's ns.WeekOf, which bins by the reset's instant); days are its seven dates with their moves (0 without any; days after d show as they stand), ringed is d, and oldBest is oldBest(d).moves (the dashed Old best line), null without one. reel (rule 18, slice 45; ported by the phones and the desktop app alone, the game making no reel; tokens.json's motion.sagaReel, sagaReveal's ms and surface.SagaReel's moveCount, which `constants.reel` repeats as these cases use them; each case gives the day's hero and heroFrom (rule 14), best (rule 6), records and unlocks (the counts of rules 12 and 13), sound (the Share window's Sound), unfilmed (the moves whose film, contract/figures/figures.json's, this surface lacks: on a phone a move newer than its app's bundled films, the game's library ahead of the app; a computer holds every film or none, desk/figures.rs filmed, so there unfilmed is all of a day's moves or none of them) and lines, the day's Quest Bill lines as the bill knows them, in any order, {move, sets (its count that day), first (the time of its first set), mark (record for a move with a record line that day, unlock for the anchor of a rung the day unlocked, else null)}): 18. the day reel: bill is the Quest Bill's order (the marked lines first, then the others, each group the most sets first, then the earlier first set, then the lower move id); the reel's moves are the hero, then the bill's moves in that order, each once, a move without its film left out, the first moveCount of them, the first of them the lead (the hero when it has its film); with none the day has no reel (share.reel.none; reel null). N moves make a reel of N x moveMs + endMs: move k (from 0) is the shot from k x moveMs for moveMs, its film from its key-pose second (figures.json's `key`) at its real tempo, wrapping at the film's end, cut hard to the next, and the end from N x moveMs for endMs the lead's film again from its key pose; every frame draws the day's Saga card in its Story layout with the reel's insets (surface.SagaCard's reelSafeTop, reelSafeBottom and reelSafeRight), its number and strip at the Saga's reveal as it stood revealFromMs before the frame's time (0 and the bare axis until revealFromMs, the total with its digitPop at revealFromMs + revealMs), its highlight slot a shot's words, which always name the move whose film plays under them: its move's Quest Bill line (line), or the day's highlight for a move with no bill line (highlight: a hero an unlock made of a move not done that day); on the end the day's highlight (highlight) only when the lead is the highlight's move (the hero, from an unlock or a record, with its film), else on a day with a record or an unlock the lead's own Quest Bill line (line: a hero with no film, so the lead is another move), and on a day with neither (a hero from most) the lead's own name (name); its sounds, with sound on (with it off the file has no audio track and sounds is empty): reveal at the number's pop (revealFromMs + revealMs), then fanfare on a best day, else record on a day with a record or an unlock, at the end's start (N x moveMs), each mixed at surface.SagaReel's gainDb; expected names bill and reel ({lead, moves [{move, from, words}], end {move, from, words}, ms, sounds [{sound, at}]}, or null; words is line, highlight or name, a shot's never name), the same on every surface. grid (rule 19, slice 45; ported by the phones and the desktop app alone; tokens.json's surface.StreakCard, which `constants.grid` repeats: width, the card's width less its two margins, and each format's height, gridStory, gridPost and gridSquare): 19. the streak card's day grid holds a cell a day of a streak of `days` days: for each column count c from 1 to days, its rows r = ceil(days / c) and its cell s = min(cellMost, width / (c + (c - 1) x gapFraction), height / (r + (r - 1) x gapFraction)); the grid takes the largest s (equal within a millionth of a point), then the fewest rows, then the fewest columns; its gap is s x gapFraction, its cells filled from the top left, a row left to right, the oldest day first and the last row's cells at its left; check is s >= checkFrom (the cell carries its check mark); expected names cols, rows, cell and gap (to 4 places) and check. Every case's expected was computed by a reference outside the repo and each boundary checked by hand.

rank.about: the first day ever: chapter 1, no earlier day and no old best, below the gate: no word, no best day

exactly at the gate: seven earlier days with a move and the day above their best (31): a best day, legendary
a tie with the old best: 52 again is no best day; the old best is the earliest day that reached 52 (6 September), not the later equal day; no day of the window has more, so the word is epic
a new best: one more than the old best, with later days in the list that the day's rules never read (a day's page reads it as it stood at its end)
the shares: a window of 20 days with 10 to 29 moves, the day's 28: one day of 20 above it (5 %): epic
the shares: a window of 20 days with 10 to 29 moves, the day's 27: two of 20 above it, exactly 10 %: not under 10, so rare
the shares: a window of 20 days with 10 to 29 moves, the day's 25: four of 20 above it (20 %): rare
the shares: a window of 20 days with 10 to 29 moves, the day's 24: five of 20 above it, exactly 25 %: not under 25, so uncommon
the shares: a window of 20 days with 10 to 29 moves, the day's 20: nine of 20 above it (45 %): uncommon
the shares: a window of 20 days with 10 to 29 moves, the day's 19: ten of 20 above it, exactly 50 %: not under 50, so common
the shares: a window of 20 days with 10 to 29 moves, the day's 10: nineteen of 20 above it, and a tie with the window's least day (10 is not above 10): common
an empty window after a long break: ten earlier days, the last of them 126 days before; the gate holds but no day lies within 56 days, so the day under the old best (40) has no word

log.about: LogPumps.build (docs/plan.md slices 34 and 44; contract/companion-api.yaml RelayedPump), the Log's and the Saga's pumps, here for a game pump and what the phone and the wrist kept of it, which both cores implement (QuestPumpCore's LogPumps.swift, the Android core's LogPumps.kt) and a probe outside the repo checks once. Each case's input: zone and dayOffsetH (the game day, as everywhere: the date in the zone of the time less dayOffsetH hours), now, rows (history rows as in cases, which HistoryPump.group makes the game's pumps), kept (the pumps the phone keeps, in contract/fixtures/backup.json's pump shape: a game pump the phone ran under the game pump's id g-<load>-<offered unix s>, source phone, with its moves, since slice 44's last review each with its slot in the game's pump and its own go (start_ms, unix ms); each move of a game pump the wrist ran as its card, <game pump id>/<slot>, source watch, since slice 44 with the card's one move from RelayedPump.gameMove, none from a watch before it); no app rows, catch-ups or sheets (no XP named), the moves' doses from the bundled contract/library.json. expected: the days newest first, each {id: its game day, ago: the game days before now's, entries: newest first}, each entry {id, at, kind, tier, count, source, watch, moves, seconds, proven, steps, peak, rise} (every other field its default: computer, pending and unwell false, appKind, link, game, matches, metres, xp and noMove null), each move {move, reps, seconds, record, hold, load, at, counted, slipped} (counted and slipped, 2026-10-19, as the top about says: false where a case leaves them out). The rules: a game pump the rows hold is the rows' pump (its tier, its pump row's count, its moves with their rows' times), and what the phone and the wrist kept of it joins it: their steps summed onto its, the highest peak with its rise, proven where its rows or a kept pump say proven, watch where a kept pump's source is watch; since slice 44's review (2026-10-17) each move the phone kept of it and each wrist card of it whose slot no performed move row of that pump has adds that move, the phone's at its own go and a card's one move at the card's go, as a move of an unheld pump below (no reps, its own seconds, no record, no load), the rows' moves, the phone's and the cards' by that time (at a tie the rows' first in their order, then the phone's in their order, then the cards by slot), and its seconds are every listed move's summed. So a pump whose pump row came without its move rows (the addon writes it as the pump opens, before any move, and the strip carries each row as it is written) lists the moves the phone and the wrist did, and each move row that lands takes its slot's place. That reads each move's slot: HistoryPump.Move carries its move row's slot (the history row's slot, which GET /v1/history serves already, so the wire is unchanged), a card its id's, and a move the phone kept its own (contract/fixtures/backup.json's pump move slot, since slice 44's last review the OfferedMove.slot it ran as); a kept move with no slot (one kept before that review) is listed only until its pump's rows come. A move the phone kept goes at its own go, start_ms / 1000, floored (backup.json's pump move start_ms, which the phone keeps beside its slot since that review: the move's first go on the phone), so its place among the rows' moves is the place its row will take once it lands: a move the phone ran after a move whose row came lists after that row; a kept move with no start_ms (one kept before) lists at its pump's first go (the pump's start_ms / 1000, floored). A game pump the rows do not hold yet stands under the id and the time its rows' pump will have (row-<offered>, at the offered time its id ends in), kind game, source game, tier 0, joined alike; since slice 44 it lists every move the phone and the wrist kept of it: the phone's kept moves, each at its own go (as above, else its pump's first go), and each card's one move, at that card's go, all by that time (at a tie the phone's first in their order, then the cards by slot), a kept move with no reps (its count is typed in the game), its own seconds, no record and no load; its count is the phone's kept moves plus one for each card (a card with no move counts as the move it was), its seconds every kept pump's seconds summed. So a game pump done only on the watch lists its moves (names and seconds) before its rows land, the Saga counts them on their own game days, and the rows' pump that replaces it holds the same moves. Until slice 44 a pump the rows did not hold listed only the phone's kept moves, counted the phone's moves or else the cards, and took the phone's seconds or else the cards'; until its review a pump the rows held listed its move rows alone and summed their seconds, and until its last review it listed no move the phone kept; until the fix after that review every move the phone kept went at its pump's first go, so while slot 0's move row had come and slot 1's had not, the phone's slot 1 move listed before slot 0's row.

the same phone-only pump (its kept moves with their slots and their own goes, the plank's 49.5 s after the squat's) once its pump row and slot 0's move row came and slot 1's not yet (slice 44's last review, the fix after it, 2026-10-17): slot 0's squat is its row's (the typed 12 at its row's time, 1792522866) and the phone's kept squat adds nothing, slot 1's plank is the phone's kept one at its own go (1792522880), after the squat's row as its own row will be, and slot 2's jumping jacks the card's at its go; the same moves, count and seconds as in case 6 and as before the rows came. a counted set worded as the game's Log words it (2026-10-19, the program's double-check): four game pumps, their rows alone.
